external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A customer who browses the storefront and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: Third-party payment processor that settles payments and calls back on settlement.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: Node service on Cloud Run; the only internet-exposed component. Terminates shopper sessions and receives the processor's settlement webhook.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run. It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

processes.name: order service
processes.description: Python worker that captures orders, persists them, and writes receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network; it is not exposed outside.

data_stores.name: orders db
data_stores.description: PostgreSQL database holding orders, shopper addresses and card last-four.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: Cloud Storage bucket holding one receipt per completed order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: place order
data_flows.description: Shopper submits an order over an authenticated session.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie; we have not rolled out MFA for shopper accounts yet.
data_flows.authentication: session cookie issued after email and password login; no MFA
data_flows.data_description: order contents, shipping address, card last-four

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: Processor POSTs a settlement callback marking an order paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid. I would have to check how that callback is authenticated.

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: Storefront API forwards a submitted order into the core zone for capture.
data_flows.source_excerpt: There is no auth on that gRPC call — the order service accepts anything that can reach it
data_flows.data_description: order contents, shopper identifiers, shipping address

data_flows.name: read write orders
data_flows.description: Order service reads and writes order rows.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a single application account that has full read/write. The password comes from an environment variable on the worker.
data_flows.authentication: single shared application account with full read/write; password from an environment variable
data_flows.data_description: order rows, shipping addresses, card last-four

data_flows.name: append receipt
data_flows.description: Order service writes one receipt object per completed order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: That is on TLS with the order service's own service account
data_flows.data_description: receipt recording the order written and that the order service wrote it

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: Everything outside the storefront's control: shoppers and the card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: storefront dmz
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-exposed tier holding the storefront API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run. It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: core services
trust_boundaries.description: Internal network holding the order service and its data.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network; it is not exposed outside.

assumptions.assumption: The order service is reachable only from inside the core network, not from the internet.
assumptions.basis: Described as "in our core network; it is not exposed outside".
